subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `direct.*.tools` be a supported hard tool-enforcement contract, or should the schema/docs reject or diagnose it as unsupported?
rationale: The current config surface implies per-DM tool restriction, but enforcing or retiring it changes a security-sensitive operator contract for shared Telegram agents.

options.title: Enforce direct tool policy
options.body: Add a DM-aware policy resolver that applies specific and wildcard `direct` policy with sender precedence, account scope, and regression/live Telegram proof.

options.title: Retire the config surface
options.body: Remove or diagnose `direct.*.tools` / `toolsBySender` and document that per-DM tool policy is unsupported rather than silently accepting it.

recommendation.title: Enforce direct tool policy
recommendation.body: Add a DM-aware policy resolver that applies specific and wildcard `direct` policy with sender precedence, account scope, and regression/live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-policy commits and the security-sensitive resolver boundary make this the strongest available routing candidate from history.
